en: Now that we saw Deno in action, and now that
we see how it generally works,
there is one annoying thing, and that's the
fact that my IDE does not like this global
Deno object. It's there, we can use it,
otherwise our script wouldn't have worked,
but my IDE does not think so.
And the reason for that is that this project
setup doesn't give any hint to Visual Studio
Code that this should work. Now maybe this
might change in the future and Visual Studio
Code might have some built-in Deno support.
At the moment it does not, but we can change
this because the good thing is that Visual
Studio Code is quite extensible.
We can install an extension by going to
View,
Extensions,
and there you can search for Deno
and you'll find this Deno support for VS
Code by JustJavec, or however this should be
pronounced.
We can install this, and this will basically
install an extension to Visual Studio Code
which makes Visual Studio Code aware of
Deno.
Actually, development is moving fast, and
only a couple of days after I recorded this,
this Deno extension is already deprecated,
and you should use the official Denoland VS
Code Deno extension, which is this one here.
So make sure you you don't use this one by
JustJavac but instead use this extension
here to, well, follow along with Deno
development. The other extension still works
and at the point of time I'm recording this,
unfortunately, it even works better than the
official one but going forward, that of
course should not be the case so I recommend
going with that official extension here from
Denoland.
And if we now go back to the Explorer,
and close this.
Now you see the error is gone. And not just
that, if I now add a dot after Deno, I even
get suggestions here. And all these core
APIs which you see here
in the Deno documentation
are now also shown here directly in Visual
Studio Code. Something like writeFile or
readFile,
that's now all built in. And if we now call
such a function, we even get the information
which we find here in the docs,
right here in the IDE in this popup, which
of course is very convenient to work with.
So therefore now we got a much nicer
development experience with this extra Deno
extension.
And with that, we made a huge step forward
and now we're really prepared to start
working with Deno
and dig deeper into it.
